title: trip-pocket-burn-rate-local-vendors
content:
Purpose: compact personal playbook for conference travel — focus on controlling per-trip burn, vendor handoffs (AV, shipping, local SIM), and clean expense artifacts for fast reimbursement. Mostly a scratchpad; keep updated after each trip.

Trip summary (quick):
- Event: European Dev Summit — booth + two onsite demos
- Dates: arrival 2026-03-16, depart 2026-03-20
- Primary card: Redwood Corporate Amex (last4 4321) for vendor charges; personal CC only for incidental tips/taxis if corporate maxed.
- Per-diem target: €70/day (meals + small taxis) unless team pre-approves higher. Keep receipts for any single >€25 purchase.

Expense capture rules (my quick checklist):
- Photograph receipt immediately; filename: YYYY-MM-DD_vendor_amount_cc-last4 (e.g., 2026-03-17-deli-23.50-4321.jpg)
- For food: itemize attendees (if paying for others, list names and team)
- For taxis/rides: include pickup+drop addresses when possible
- Hotel folio: request itemized folio at checkout even if company paid; include folio in report
- Shipping/booth: get invoice from vendor (PDF), confirm VAT handling and whether Redwood is billed net or gross
- Add short note to expense: event name + booth code (e.g., EDS-23 booth B12)
- Submit to Expensify within 5 business days post-trip; link Concur/Finance ticket if larger than €1,000

Quick upload metadata template (copy into expense entry):
- Expense title: "EDS-23 — taxi / demo materials / dinner"
- Date: 2026-03-17
- Amount: €23.50
- Payment method: Corporate AMEX 4321
- Notes: "airport -> hotel, shared with Liam O'Connor (team demo prep)"

Local vendor & SIM notes (shortlist):
- Mobile: DingTel kiosk — Airport arrivals (Terminal 1, stall 3). SIM kit 10GB 30-day = €18. Top-up via Credit Card or cash. Ask for eSIM if phone unlocked — saves kiosk wait. Phone: +353 1 555 0199, email: sales@dingtel.ie
- Local transport card: Leap Card vendor at Info Desk — buy if using public for >2 trips per day
- Booth freight (local handler): Emerald Event Logistics
  - Contact: Aoife Brennan, +353 87 224 9981, aoife.brennan@emerald-ev.com
  - Typical charges: booth unload €120; overnight storage €45/day; small-item drayage €25
- AV on-site: PixelWorks AudioVisual (onsite lead: Marco Silva, +44 7702 334455, schedule AV test for day-before at 4pm)

Vendor invoice checklist (ask vendor to confirm in email):
- Company name and address
- VAT number (if applicable)
- Description of service + date(s)
- Total amount and currency (explicit)
- Preferred payment method and banking details

Pre-departure items (my go-to checklist):
- [ ] Order SIM / eSIM QR (if remote) or add to arrivals pickup note
- [ ] Confirm booth crate arrival slot with Emerald (ETA + contact cell)
- [ ] Confirm Marco (AV) test time and HDMI adaptors required
- [ ] Pre-load expense folder on phone (folder: EDS-23-Receipts) and test upload to Expensify
- [ ] Export corporate card statement for the trip dates (screenshot)

Onsite ops quick notes:
- Badge pickup: bring passport (photo id) + confirmation email; badges often only at main registration desk; allow 45–60 minutes first morning
- Demo devices: bring 2 USB-C -> HDMI adapters, 1 dongle for Mac, power strip with EU sockets and local adaptor; label all chargers with masking tape + name
- Booth handoff: leave one contact card visible (my name + phone + slack handle). If leaving early, hand physical keys to Aoife and confirm final crate count in Slack channel #eds-booth-ops

Receipt naming / archiving (practical):
- Photos: JPG, phone HDR off if possible to reduce file size
- File name pattern: 2026-03-17_vendor_short-what_amount_cc4321.jpg
- Upload order: immediately to Expensify, then to Drive folder: Drive -> Travel -> EDS-23 -> receipts (I use screenshots + original photo)

Slack & comms templates (copy/paste):
- To vendor (email): "Hi [Name], confirming: Emerald will deliver booth crate between 08:00–10:00 on 2026-03-16 to Hall B. Please confirm delivery window and on-site contact. Invoice and VAT details appreciated. Thanks, Priya / Redwood Inference"
- Quick Slack (team): "@booth-team arriving 16th — Aoife (Emerald) confirmed unload 08:30. Marco (AV) scheduled test 15th 16:00. Ping me for last-minute pickup or keys."

Common expense gotchas (notes to self):
- Taxis w/o receipts: prefer using company ride account (if possible). If forced to use cash, get driver name/plate and Google Maps route screenshot and add a note in expense.
- Shared meals: write names + roles; avoid claiming individual alcohol >€50 without pre-approval
- Currency conversions: record exact card FX amount; do not rely on rough manual conversions in the report

Emergency + backup contacts (local):
- Redwood on-call travel: travel-ops@redwood.ai (internal) — also post in #travel-ops for visibility
- Local embassy (emergency passport): +353 1 677 0011 (for US consular services in Dublin) — check website before loss
- Personal ICE (in case of hospital): Liam O'Connor +44 7700 900111

Post-trip wrap & retro notes (to update after return):
- Actual per-day spend vs target (track on a small sheet): meals, local transport, vendor fees, incidentals
- What vendor quotes were inaccurate or had hidden fees (track and add to vendor notes)
- Any receipts missing: chase vendor for invoice or credit card evidence

Unresolved questions to follow-up:
- Does Finance want shipping vendors pre-approved for VAT reclaim? (flag to Sasha)
- Can we get a small petty cash float for booth incidentals to avoid personal CC use?

Quick metrics I track (for my own burn-rate sense):
- Pre-booked vendor spend (shipping + AV): target <= €1,200
- Pay-on-arrival vendor spend (local drayage, storage): target <= €250
- Variable (meals/taxis): ~€70/day

Notes-to-self: keep this doc minimal and re-use filename pattern for all EMEA trips (change EDS-23 to event code). After trip, prune vendor list (who was reliable) and add invoice samples to Drive folder for easier Finance review.
